reproduction_target: Age-dependent multi-omics characterisation of Pacific oyster (Magallana gigas) permissiveness to POMS (OsHV-1 muVar). Computational target: (i) EM-seq DNA-methylation pipeline - FastQC v.0.53 -> TrimGalore! v.0.6.10 -> Bismark v0.24.2 (bismark_genome_preparation / bismark / deduplicate_bismark / bismark_methylation_extractor) against M. gigas GCA_902806645.1 plus lambda spike-in conversion control -> methylKit v.1.24.0 (8X common CpGs, median normalisation) -> biomaRt v.2.54.1 gene coordinates -> data.table v.1.14.8 foverlaps and per-gene-body mean methylation; (ii) RNA-seq pipeline - Trim Galore! v.0.6.7 -> FastQC v.0.11.9 -> STAR v.2.7.10b -> HTSeq v.0.9.1 on the host genome, and Bowtie2 v2.3.4.3 -> HTSeq-count on the OsHV-1 muVar genome KY242785.1 with a custom ORF-size/depth normalisation formula -> DESeq2 v.1.42.1 (count filter <=15, vst, FDR<0.05); (iii) targeted GC-MS metabolomics processing - internal-standard normalisation -> MetaboAnalystR v.4.0.0 (IQR<25 filter, quantile normalisation, log transform); (iv) integrative/statistical layer - R v.4.4.1, ggplot2 v.3.5.1, survival v.3.2-11 / survminer v.0.4.9 Kaplan-Meier + Mantel-Cox + coxph, stats v.4.4.1 / car shapiro-Levene-ANOVA-TukeyHSD on viral loads, WGCNA v.1.73 module detection across the three omics layers, GO_MWU (github.com/z0on/GO_MWU, unversioned) BP-GO enrichment on kME vectors, FELLA v.1.22.0 KEGG diffusion enrichment, KEGGREST v.1.46.0 pathway-gene retrieval, and the bespoke cross-referencing of KEGG-pathway genes against the transcriptomic DE tables for seven focal pathways. Oyster family production, OsHV-1 muVar suspension production, cohabitation infection challenge and survival monitoring, sampling/nucleic-acid extraction, qPCR viral-load quantification, EM-seq and RNA-seq library construction and sequencing (IntegraGen SA), and metabolite extraction/derivatisation/GC-MS acquisition (MAMMA platform) are W (out of computational-reproduction scope).
granularity_note: Stage-1 prose-only read of the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML (fetched 2026-07-27, HTTP 200, 289,129 bytes; title phrase 'Counterintuitive Reversal' verified present in the fetched file). The paper has a conventional Methods section with named tools, explicit version strings and explicit command-line/function parameters for most steps, but NO Code Availability section and NO source repository of any kind. One step per named tool invocation, following the guide Step-1 anchor; where the same tool is invoked twice on different data (FastQC, Trim Galore!, HTSeq) the invocations are kept as separate steps because their stated versions and parameters differ between the EM-seq and RNA-seq branches. Bespoke, unnamed-implementation operations that the prose describes but does not attach to a released script (custom viral-count normalisation formula, per-gene-body methylation averaging, KEGG-gene cross-referencing, GO-term regrouping, PCA outlier removal, figure assembly) are scored as separate C-steps with Code=0. The GO annotation database construction (TransDecoder / ORSON / OmicsBox v.3.4.5) is inherited from Duperret et al. 2025 and is scored as one C-step because its output is a required input here. 7 wet-lab steps recorded as W and excluded from |S|.

steps.label: Wet-lab: production of four biparental full-sibling M. gigas families (H2D, F14R, F11N, F14V) at the Ifremer Argenton hatchery (2020), nursery rearing under biosecured conditions at Bouin, and acclimation of the 4-, 16- and 28-month-old offspring at 23 C for 15 days; pathogen-free status confirmed by OsHV-1 muVar qPCR and Vibrio counts

Wet-lab: production and quantification of the OsHV-1 muVar viral suspension (Schikorski et al. 2011 protocol; sequential centrifugation 3,000 x g / 10,000 g, 0.45 and 0.22 um filtration; genomic-unit quantification by qPCR on a Stratagene Mx3005P)

Wet-lab: experimental infection by cohabitation with OsHV-1 muVar-injected donor oysters, in three independent challenge experiments covering the three age classes, with 4-month-old NSI donors and recipients as controls
Wet-lab: survival monitoring of the four families at 4, 16 and 28 months and sampling time-course, with tissue collection, flash freezing and storage at -80 C
Wet-lab: gDNA/RNA extraction and qPCR quantification of OsHV-1 muVar viral DNA load in the extracted gDNA samples

Wet-lab: NEBNext Enzymatic Methyl-seq (EM-seq) library preparation from 100 ng gDNA with unmethylated lambda and methylated pUC19 spike-ins, and NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA library preparation; Illumina NovaSeq sequencing (150 bp PE for EM-seq, 100 bp PE for RNA-seq) by IntegraGen SA (Evry, France)

Wet-lab: targeted metabolomics at the MAMMA platform - 20 mg powder in ice-cold methanol with MES and mixed internal standards, SPE purification, SpeedVac drying, methoxyamine/MSTFA derivatisation by PAL autosampler, Agilent 8890 GC with DB-MS+DG column and 5977B MSD in dynamic MRM mode

EM-seq raw-read quality control with FastQC (v.0.53 as printed in the paper; note this version string does not correspond to any released FastQC version and is likely a typo for 0.11.x/0.12.x) - no parameters stated, defaults implied
EM-seq adapter/quality trimming with TrimGalore! v.0.6.10: '-q 30 --paired --clip_R1 5 --clip_R2 5 --Illumina', followed by a second trimming round with default parameters to remove residual adapters
Bisulfite-conversion of the M. gigas reference genome (GCA_902806645.1) with Bismark v0.24.2 'bismark_genome_preparation'; underlying aligner (bowtie2/HISAT2) and its version not stated
Alignment of trimmed EM-seq reads to the bisulfite-converted M. gigas genome with the Bismark v0.24.2 'bismark' function: '-q -N 0 --score_min L,0,-0.4'
Duplicate removal with 'deduplicate_bismark' and methylation calling with 'bismark_methylation_extractor' ('--no_overlap --cutoff 8'), Bismark v0.24.2

Enzymatic-conversion-efficiency control: the same Bismark pipeline applied to the bacteriophage lambda spike-in genome, with samples below 98.0% conversion discarded (reported efficiency 99.18% +/- 3.62%, Table S4); the lambda reference accession and the pUC19 control handling are not stated

Methylation-matrix construction with methylKit v.1.24.0: retention of CpGs common to all samples with minimum coverage 8X and 'median' normalisation; the destranding, tiling and any differential-methylation test are not specified (age association is instead handled downstream by WGCNA)

Retrieval of genic coordinates (chromosome, start, end) for all coding genes of M. gigas with biomaRt v.2.54.1 - the mart, host, dataset and Ensembl/Ensembl-Metazoa release are not stated, so the queried resource is an unpinned live service

Intersection of gene-body coordinates with CpG coordinates using the 'foverlaps' function of data.table v.1.14.8, followed by per-gene averaging of methylation values across multiple CpGs within the same gene body - implemented in an in-house script that is not deposited
RNA-seq read trimming with Trim Galore! v.0.6.7: '-q 30 --illumina --stringency 1 -e 0.1 --length 35'
RNA-seq read quality assessment before and after trimming with FastQC v.0.11.9 - no parameters stated, defaults implied

Alignment of trimmed RNA-seq PE reads to the M. gigas genome (GCA_902806645.1) with STAR v.2.7.10b: '--runMode alignReads --outSAMmapqUnique 60 --outSAMattributes All'; the genomeGenerate index build, the annotation GTF/GFF used for splice junctions and its release are not stated
Host gene-level read counting with HTSeq v.0.9.1: '--stranded reverse -t gene -i ID -m union -q --minequal 10'
Alignment of trimmed RNA-seq reads to the OsHV-1 muVar genome (KY242785.1) with Bowtie2 v2.3.4.3 to quantify viral transcriptional activity - no bowtie2 flags, preset or index-build recipe stated
Viral ORF-level counting with HTSeq-count (v.0.9.1), same parameters as the host counting except feature type 'CDS' and ID attribute 'product'

Custom normalisation of viral raw counts by ORF length and sequencing depth ('The viral raw counts were normalized based on the formula: .' - the formula itself is rendered only as a display equation that is empty in the fetched JATS body, and the implementing script is not deposited); method attributed to de Lorgeril et al. 2018

Transcriptomic data treatment and differential expression with DESeq2 v.1.42.1: filtering of the raw count matrix (counts <= 15 across all samples), library-size normalisation, variance-stabilising transformation via 'vst', reported fold changes at FDR < 0.05 with 4-month-old oysters as reference - the design formula, the test used (Wald/LRT) and the shrinkage setting are not stated
Metabolomics processing with MetaboAnalystR v.4.0.0: internal-standard peak-area normalisation, IQR cutoff < 25 removing 10% of compounds, quantile normalisation and log transformation

Survival analysis in R v.4.4.1: Kaplan-Meier curves via 'survfit' (survival v.3.2-11) plotted with 'ggsurvplot' (survminer v.0.4.9), Mantel-Cox log-rank tests against the 4-month-old reference group within each family, and Cox proportional-hazards models via 'coxph' - the underlying per-individual mortality records are not deposited (available 'from the corresponding authors on reasonable request')

Viral DNA-load and viral RNA-transcription statistics: 'shapiro.test' from stats v.4.4.1 and 'leveneTest' from car for normality/homoscedasticity, one-way ANOVA via 'aov' across age groups, Tukey HSD via 'TukeyHSD' - the car package version is not stated and the qPCR/count input tables are not deposited

Weighted correlation network analysis with WGCNA v.1.73 applied per family to each of the three omics layers (methylation, expression, metabolites), trait = age recoded 1/2/3, module-trait Pearson correlation at P < 0.05, network parameters 'maxBlockSize = 30,000, networkType = signed, TOMtype = signed, mergeCutHeight = 0.25, minModuleSize = 100'; the soft-power threshold is described as chosen for scale-free topology but its value is not reported, and the merging of same-direction modules is described only in prose

GO Biological-Process enrichment on the kME vectors (all 30,418 coding genes, 0 assigned outside modules) with the GO_MWU package (github.com/z0on/GO_MWU): 'largest = 0.5, smallest = 10, clusterCutHeight = 0.25, Module = TRUE, Alternative = g', significance at P.adj < 0.05 - no GO_MWU version, tag or commit is given, and the GO annotation table used is the one inherited from Duperret et al. 2025 rather than a deposited file

Metabolite pathway reconstruction and enrichment with FELLA v.1.22.0 using a diffusion algorithm over KEGG entities (reactions, enzymes, modules) on the age-associated metabolites from the WGCNA modules - the KEGG build date used to construct the FELLA graph, the diffusion approximation and the significance cutoff are not stated

Retrieval of genes annotated to the significantly enriched KEGG pathways by querying the live KEGG service with KEGGREST v.1.46.0 against the M. gigas ('crg') organism database - KEGG is queried as a rolling online resource with no release/date recorded

Bespoke integration step: compilation of all genes annotated to the enriched KEGG pathways and cross-referencing against the transcriptomic differential-expression tables for seven focal pathways (crg00020, crg00230, crg00240, crg00250, crg00330, crg00430, crg00480), plus the metabolite-gene concordance mapping used to build Figures 6/S7/S8 - no script released and no selection rule stated beyond 'we focused our validation on seven key pathways'

Manual/bespoke regrouping of the significant BP GO-terms from GO_MWU into broader categories 'based on the Gene Ontology database' (result tabulated in Table S3) - no algorithm, no semantic-similarity tool, no script

Quality-control outlier removal: 'samples falling outside the 95% confidence ellipse in PCA were considered outliers and subsequently removed' - the PCA implementation (package, function, input transformation, which omics layers it was applied to) is not named, and the list of removed samples is not reported
Figure generation: plots 'primarily generated' with ggplot2 v.3.5.1 under R v.4.4.1, plus the multi-panel integrative figures (Figures 2-6, S1-S8) whose assembly scripts are not released

Inherited input: the GO-term gene annotation database required by GO_MWU, constructed in Duperret et al. 2025 - coding sequences extracted with TransDecoder (no version), annotated with ORSON (BLASTX vs Uniprot-SwissProt, InterProScan domain prediction; no versions, no database release), validated with the commercial OmicsBox software v.3.4.5, and 'further enriched with immune-related terms' by an unspecified manual procedure

headline.static_readiness: 0/29 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 19/29 (66%) RI, 10/29 (34%) NI. This paper is unusually well-pinned at the prose level and unusually empty at the artifact level. On the positive side: all sequencing and metabolomics data are deposited and live (ENA PRJEB86647 umbrella, PRJEB105019 EM-seq, PRJEB105132 RNA-seq, MetaboLights MTBLS13463 - all HTTP 200 and public on 2026-07-27), both reference genomes are given as versioned accessions (GCA_902806645.1, KY242785.1), and 19 of 21 named software components carry an exact version string with the actual command-line flags or function arguments printed in the Methods. On the negative side, the binding constraint is the total absence of code: there is no Code Availability section, and no GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Zenodo/Software Heritage/OSF/CodeOcean URL appears anywhere in the full text (the single 'github.com' occurrence is the citation of the third-party GO_MWU package). Every step is therefore capped at Code=1 (reconstructable from prose) at best, and the ten steps whose implementation is bespoke or unnamed (per-gene methylation averaging, the custom viral-count normalisation formula, the KEGG-gene cross-referencing, the GO-term regrouping, the unnamed PCA outlier filter, figure assembly, the inherited annotation-database build) drop to Code=0 and NI. Version is capped at 1 for every step by rubric Delta-2: the pins are scattered prose pins with no interpreter/channel/platform closure (no renv.lock, no conda environment, no container, no sessionInfo). No step can reach R-star at Stage 1, and because no code artifact exists to inspect, this paper would gain nothing from a Stage-2 code read either.
headline.coverage: 29 computational steps assessed from a complete conventional Methods section; 7 wet-lab steps recorded as W and excluded. Computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 29/36 = 81%. Prose coverage of the pipeline is high (tools, versions and flags are printed for most invocations); artifact coverage is zero for code and complete for primary data.

gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked. The paper has no Code Availability section; the Data availability statement covers only ENA and MetaboLights deposits and closes with 'Complementary information is available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request'. A case-insensitive scan of the full JATS text for github/gitlab/bitbucket/zenodo/softwareheritage/osf/codeocean returns exactly one hit, the third-party citation 'GO_MWU package (github.com/z0on/GO_MWU)', which is a tool reference and not this study's code.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the EM-seq, RNA-seq, metabolomics and integration scripts in a public repository with an archived tagged release (Zenodo DOI), and add a Code Availability statement pointing at it.

gaps.where: C9, C16, C25, C26, C27, C28 (and C29 inherited)
gaps.missing: The bespoke parts of the analysis exist only as prose descriptions: the foverlaps-based CpG-to-gene-body assignment and per-gene averaging, the custom viral-count normalisation by ORF length and sequencing depth (whose formula is a display equation that is empty in the fetched JATS body), the compilation and cross-referencing of KEGG-pathway genes against the DE tables, the regrouping of BP GO-terms into broader categories, the unnamed PCA-based outlier filter, and the figure-assembly code. The custom GO-term annotation database inherited from Duperret et al. 2025 is likewise not deposited with this paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Release these scripts and deposit the derived intermediate tables (methylation-per-gene matrix, normalised viral ORF counts, DE tables, the GO annotation database) as supplementary data files with stable identifiers.

gaps.where: Software environment for all 29 steps; specific missing pins at C1, C8, C20, C22, C29
gaps.missing: No environment closure of any kind: no renv.lock, no conda/mamba environment file, no container image or digest, no requirements file, no sessionInfo dump, no platform declaration. The version information is scattered prose pins only (R v.4.4.1, ggplot2 v.3.5.1, survival v.3.2-11, survminer v.0.4.9, stats v.4.4.1, WGCNA v.1.73, methylKit v.1.24.0, biomaRt v.2.54.1, data.table v.1.14.8, DESeq2 v.1.42.1, MetaboAnalystR v.4.0.0, FELLA v.1.22.0, KEGGREST v.1.46.0, TrimGalore! v.0.6.10 and v.0.6.7, Bismark v0.24.2, STAR v.2.7.10b, HTSeq v.0.9.1, Bowtie2 v2.3.4.3, FastQC v.0.11.9, OmicsBox v.3.4.5), so Version is capped at 1 with subtier exact_pins_partial. Specific version gaps: GO_MWU has no version/tag/commit; the car package has no version; TransDecoder and ORSON have no versions; the aligner underlying bismark_genome_preparation (bowtie2 or HISAT2) is never named; and the printed 'FastQC (v.0.53)' for the EM-seq branch does not match any released FastQC version and conflicts with 'FastQC software (v.0.11.9)' used in the RNA-seq branch.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a lockfile (renv.lock plus a conda-lock for the command-line tools) or a container with a recorded digest, declare the platform, and correct/reconcile the two conflicting FastQC version strings.

gaps.where: C8 (biomaRt), C22 (GO annotation), C23 (FELLA/KEGG), C24 (KEGGREST), C29 (Uniprot-SwissProt, InterPro)
gaps.missing: Every reference resource other than the two genome accessions is consumed as a rolling online service with no release recorded: the biomaRt mart/host/dataset and Ensembl release are unstated, KEGG is queried live through KEGGREST and through the FELLA graph build with no KEGG release date, and the Uniprot-SwissProt and InterProScan releases behind the inherited GO annotation are unstated. These resources change continuously, so an identical re-run is not defined even in principle.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the release/date of each external database used (Ensembl release, KEGG release, Uniprot-SwissProt release, InterPro version) and deposit frozen copies of the derived annotation tables alongside the code.

gaps.where: C19, C20 (survival and viral-load statistics); sample-to-run mapping for C1-C18
gaps.missing: The phenotype-level data underpinning Figure 1 - per-individual or per-tank mortality records for the four families at three ages, and the qPCR viral DNA loads - are not deposited in any repository and are covered only by the 'available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request' clause. In addition, the paper does not print a sample-to-ENA-run mapping table, so the assignment of the deposited EM-seq and RNA-seq runs to family (H2D/F14R), age (4/16/28 months) and replicate must be inferred from the ENA sample metadata rather than from the paper.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the survival and qPCR tables as machine-readable supplementary files and publish an explicit sample-to-accession mapping table.

gaps.missing: OmicsBox v.3.4.5 is commercial licensed software required to reproduce the validation step of the GO annotation database. It is version-pinned, so it is scored license-gated (Version=1 in isolation) rather than unknown, but combined with the absent code and the unversioned TransDecoder/ORSON/BLASTX/InterProScan components the step cannot exceed NI.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the finished GO annotation table so that reproducing the downstream enrichment does not require re-running the proprietary annotation step.

gaps.missing: The GO annotation database is externalised to a companion paper (Duperret et al. 2025) and summarised in this paper only as a three-clause 'Briefly, ...' sentence. Its reproduction depends entirely on artifacts of that other publication, whose availability is not asserted here.
gaps.how_to_close: Either deposit the annotation product with this paper or cite the exact deposited artifact (DOI/accession) of the companion study.

gaps.missing: Family production and rearing, viral-suspension production, the cohabitation infection challenge, survival monitoring and sampling, nucleic-acid extraction and qPCR, EM-seq/RNA-seq library construction and sequencing, and metabolite extraction/derivatisation/GC-MS acquisition are wet-lab and out of scope for computational reproducibility. They are documented in reasonable protocol detail with method citations, but they are not part of |S|.
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - out of scope by rubric Step 5 (recorded for coverage accounting only).
